title: Alan Ornelas leaves his mark on Martin baseball with dominant 2025 - NewsBreak
text: Alejandro Garza has coached in the Martin baseball program for 12 years now. He's seen some ballplayers go through the Tigers organization. One of the best to come through during those 12 years was 2025 graduate Alan Ornelas. "He's been a leader for us for four years," Garza said. "This year was similar to last year. We had our backs against the wall and we needed a big win. Alan had the ball and he'd get us that win. Alan came through for us the majority of the season. That's what we expected from him. He knew what he needed to do. He's been through the pressure and that's when he's at his best." Ornelas was one of Laredo's best all-around players in 2025. As a second-team All-City selection and first-team District 30-5A selection as a pitcher, Ornelas was consistent on the mound and at the plate. The right-handed hurler posted a 2.06 ERA and an 8-2 record with a team-high 52 strikeouts across 54 1/3 innings pitched. He had five outings with no earned runs allowed. At the plate, Ornelas was just as deadly. He tallied team highs in hits (31), RBIs (18) and doubles (nine), while batting .463 with a 1.152 OPS. Behind the powerful play of Ornelas, Martin reached the 5A playoffs for the second season in a row at 14-11-1 overall and 9-7 in district action. "We've had some good players come and go," Garza said of his 12 seasons so far at Martin. The first 10 were spent as an assistant coach. "It's special at Martin. You get a lot of support from the older players. They come help us out. They're always supporting. It's different with Alan since I coached him as a head coach and assistant coach. Having him these past two years, he's up there. He knew what we expected from him. We wouldn't have made the playoffs without him." Ornelas' impact goes far beyond the impressive statsheet. When he was on the mound or at the plate, the Tigers felt like they had a chance in any situation. "It's a big impact for all of us. We believe all the time we can win," Garza said. "When he has the ball or is up to bat, we know good things can happen. When Alan was on the mound, our best defense was out there." He added, "It was always a positive when Alan was on the mound. It seems like those guys had more pep to their step when he had the ball." Ornelas' 2025 added to a stellar four-year career at Martin. In 102 games played, Ornelas collected 71 hits, 33 RBIs and 11 doubles with a .280 average as a four-year starter at the plate. On the mound across three seasons, he was 14-11 with a 4.43 ERA and 102 strikeouts. The leap he took from a solid 2024 to 2025 propelled him to new heights. He struck out nearly twice as many batters, tallied twice as many hits and doubled his batting average. According to Garza, the leap came from Ornelas' hard work. "This guy has been a hard worker since he got in," Garza said. "He comes in and knows what he needs to do." With Frankie Cantu being banged up for most of the 2025 season, Ornelas became Martin's ace for home games. Garza said, with that added responsibility, that Ornelas would come in a few days ahead of a start to get ready for the game. "He knows he needs to come in on Saturday if he's going to pitch on Tuesday to put in that extra work," Garza said. "It's easy for us coaches knowing this guy knows what he needs to do. We don't have to question him. He's always done the hard work." As of right now, Ornelas has no college baseball plans. Garza said Ornelas wants to focus on his studies in law enforcement and that he was in the top 10% of students in his graduating class at Martin. Ornelas won the Triple A award at Martin every year, which stands for Academics, Attendance and Attitude. Ornelas was the leader of a special 2025 class for Martin, which also included Ruben Hernandez, Fabian Reyna, Aldo Alarcon, Edgar Garcia, Diego Blanco and Victor Torres. Garza was emotional when reflecting on what that group meant to him and the program. "It seems surreal with these guys who were four year starters," Garza said. "It's going to be a bit strange come August and these guys not walking in the locker room. They knew exactly what we expected from the program. I know these guys are going to do great things in the future. They know they have a special place with us."
